G6500:
ἀποτέμνω
I. to cut off, sever, Il., Hdt., attic:—Pass., τὴν γλῶτταν ἀποτμηθείς having his tongue cut out, Aeschin.
2. to sever, divide, in a geographical sense, Hdt.:—Pass., of troops, to be cut off from the main body, Xen.
II. Mid. to cut off for oneself, Il.; c. gen. to cut off a bit of a thing, Hdt.
2. to cut off, so as to appropriate, βοῦς Hhymn., Hdt.; Φοινίκης ἀπ. to have a slice or portion of Phoenicia, Theocr.; ἀπ. τῶν Ἀθηναίων to cut off power from the Athenians, Thuc.
G6503:
ἀποτρέχω
I. to run off or away, Hdt., attic
II. to run hard, of one training for a race, Ar.
G6506:
ἀποτυγχάνω
I. to fail in hitting or gaining, to miss, lose, c. gen., Xen., etc.
2. Pass., τὰ ἀποτετευγμένα things not come to pass, Luc.
II. absol. to miss one's object, to be unlucky, fail, Xen.: to miss the truth, err, id.:—c. inf. to fail to do, id.
G6508:
ἀποφαίνω
I. to shew fort, display, produce, Hdt., Ar.
II. to make known, declare, Hdt.: to give evidence of a thing, id.
2. to shew by reasoning, shew, represent as doing or being, c. part., id.; and with part. omitted, ἀπ. ἑωϋτὸν αἴτιον (sc. ὄντα) id.; so, ἀπ. τινα ἐχθρόν Dem.
3. c. acc. et inf. to represent that, Plat.; so, ἀπ. ὡς . . , ὅτι . . , Hdt., Thuc.
III. to give an account of, τὴν οὐσίαν Dem.: to pay in money to the treasury, id.
IV. to render or make so and so, Ar.
2. to appoint to an office, Plat.
B. Mid. to display something of one's own, Aesch. Plat.: absol. to make a display of oneself, shew off, Xen.
2. to produce evidence, Hdt.
3. ἀποφαίνεσθαι γνώμην to declare one's opinion, id., attic:— absol. to give an opinion, Hdt., attic. Hence
II. used like Act., Plat., Xen.
G6509:
ἀπόφθεγμα [ἀποφθέγγομαι]
a terse pointed saying, an apophthegm, Xen.
G6510:
ἀποφορά [ἀποφέρω]
1. payment of what is due, tax, tribute, Hdt., attic
2. also, return for money spent, profit, Xen., etc.
G6512:
ἀποφυσάω
I. to blow away, Ar.
II. to breathe out life, Luc.
G6513:
ἀποχέω
to pour out or off, shed, let fall, Od.:—poet. Mid. ἀποχεύομαι, Eur.
G6514:
ἀποχώρησις [ἀποχωρέω]
a going off, retreat, Hdt., Thuc.: a place or means of safety, Hdt.
G6515:
ἄπυρος [πῦρ]
without fire, of pans and tripods, that have not yet been on the fire, fire-new, brand-new, Il.: — without fire, i. e. cold, cheerless, οἶκος Hes.:— ἄπ. χρυσίον unsmelted, Hdt.:— ἄπυρα ἱερά sacrifices in which no fire was used, Pind.; but in Aesch. sacrifices without fire, i. e. that will not burn, or unoffered, neglected:— ἄπ. ἄρδις an arrow-point not forged in fire, i. e. the sting of the gad-fly, Aesch.
G6519:
ἄπωσις [ἀπωθέω]
a driving away, Thuc.
G6522:
ἀράομαι [ἀρά]
1. to pray to a god, c. dat., Il.:—c. acc. to invoke, Od.
2. c. acc. et inf. to pray that, Il., Hdt., Soph.:—c. inf. only, to pray to be so and so, Od.
3. to pray something for one, τί τινι; sometimes in good sense, ἀρ. τινι ἀγαθά Hdt.; but usually in bad, to imprecate upon one, ἀρὰς ἀρ. τινι Soph., etc.; without an acc., ἀρᾶσθαί τινι to curse one, Eur.
4. c. inf. fut. to vow that one will or would, ἠρήσατο ῥέξειν Il.
G6523:
ἀράχνη
I. fem. of ἀράχνης, Lat. aranea, Aesch., Anth.
II. a spider's web, id.
G6524:
ἀργία [= ἀεργία]
1. idleness, laziness, Eur., Dem.
2. in good sense, rest, leisure, ἔργων from work, Plat.
G6526:
ἀργυρώνητος [ὠνέομαι]
bought with silver, Hdt., Aesch.
G6527:
ἄρδην
I. lifted up, on high, Soph., Eur.
II. taken away utterly, wholly, Lat. raptim, Aesch., Eur., etc.
G6528:
ἄρθρον [*ἄρω]
a joint, Soph.: esp. the socket of the ankle-joint, Hdt., Soph.:—in pl. joined with some other word, ἄρθρα ποδοῖν the ankles, id.; ἄρθρων ἤλυσις the legs, Eur.; ἄρθρα τῶν κύκλων the eyes, Soph.; ἄρθρα στόματος the mouth, Eur.
G6531:
ἀριθμητός [ἀριθμέω]
easily numbered, few in number, Theocr.: οὐκ ἀριθμητός held in no account, nullo numero habitus, id.
G6535:
ἁρμονία [ἁρμόζω]
I. a fastening to keep ship-planks together, a clamp, Od.
2. a joining, joint, between a ship's planks, τὰς ἁρμ. ἐπάκτωσαν τῆι βύβλωι caulked the joints with byblus, Hdt.
3. a frame: metaph., δύστροπος γυναικῶν ἁρμ. women's perverse temperament, Eur.
II. a covenant, agreement, in pl., Il.:— settled government, order, Aesch.
III. harmony, as a concord of sounds, first as a mythical personage, Harmonia, Music, companion of Hebe, the Graces and the Hours; child of the Muses, Hhymn., Eur.
2. metaph., harmony, concord, Plat.
G6536:
ἀροτήρ [ἀρόω]
I. a plougher, husbandman, Il., Eur.; Σκύθαι ἀροτῆρες, opp. to νομάδες, Hdt.:—adj., βοῦς ἀροτήρ a steer for ploughing, Hes.
II. metaph. a father, Eur.
G6539:
ἄρουρα [ἀρόω]
I. tilled or arable land, seed-land, cornland, Lat. arvum, and in pl. corn-lands, fields, Il.: then, generally, land, earth, id.; πατρὶς ἄρουρα father land, Od.
2. metaph. of a woman as bearing children, Aesch., Soph.
II. a measure of land in Egypt, nearly = the Roman jugerum, Hdt.
G6542:
ἀρρωστέω [ἄρρωστος]
to be weak and sickly, Xen., Dem.
G6543:
ἀρρωστία [from ἄρρωστος]
weakness, sickness, Thuc., etc.; ἀρρ.τοῦ στρατεύειν inability to serve, id.
G6545:
ἄρσις [αἴρω]
I. a raising of the foot in walking, Arist.
II. in Prosody, arsis, opp. to thesis.
G6546:
ἀρτάβη
a Persian measure, artaba, = 1 medimnus + 3 choenices, Hdt.
G6561:
ἀρχιτεκτονέω [ἀρχιτέκτων]
1. to be the architect, Plut.
2. generally, to construct, contrive, Ar.
G6564:
ἀρχός
a leader, chief, commander, Il.
G6567:
ἀσέβημα [ἀσεβής]
an impious or profane act, Thuc., Dem.
G6570:
ἀσιτέω [ἄσι—τος]
to abstain from food, fast, Eur., Plat.
G6571:
ᾆσμα [ἄιδω]
a song, a lyric ode, or lay, Plat.
G6575:
ἀστράγαλος [Deriv. uncertain.]
I. one of the neck-vertebrae, Hom.
II. the ball of the ankle joint, Lat. talus, Hdt., Theocr.
III. pl. ἀστράγαλοι, dice or agame played with dice, Il., Hdt.:—they were at first made of knuckle-bones, and never had more than four flat sides, whereas the κύβοι had six. They played with four: the best throw (βόλος), when each die came differently, was called Ἀφροδίτη, Lat. jactus Veneris; the worst, when all came alike, κύων, Lat. canis.
G6577:
ἄσυλος [σύλη]
I. safe from violence, inviolate, of persons seeking protection, Eur.:—c. gen., γάμων ἄσυλος safe from marriage, id.
II. of places, γῆν ἄσυλον παρασχεῖν to make the land a refuge, id.
G6578:
ἀσύμφορος
inconvenient, inexpedient, useless, Hes.: c. dat. inexpedient for, prejudicial to, Eur., Thuc.; also ἔς or πρός τι id.:— adv. ‐ρως, Xen.
G6583:
ἄσφαλτος
asphalt, bitumen, forming in lumps, (θρόμβοι) on the surface of the river Is near Babylon and at Ardericca near Susa, Hdt.
[Seems to be a foreign word.]
G6585:
ἄσωτος [σώζω]
I. having no hope of safety, abandoned, profligate, Lat. perditus, Soph., Arist.
II. act., ἄσωτος γένει bringing ruin on the race, fatal to it, Aesch.
G6586:
ἀτάρ
1. but, yet, Lat. at, to introduce an objection or correction, Il., attic; it always begins a sentence or clause, but is placed after the voc., Ἕκτορ, ἀτάρ που ἔφης still thou didst say, Il.:— ἀτάρ sometimes answers to μέν, more emphatic than δέ, Hom., attic
2. in attic to mark a rapid transition to another thought, Aesch., etc.; so ἀτὰρ δή Eur.
G6587:
ἀτείχιστος [τειχίζω]
1. unwalled, unfortified, Thuc.
2. not walled in, not blockaded, id.
G6588:
ἀτεκνία [From ἄτεκνος]
childlessness, Arist.
G6589:
ἀτεκνόω
to make childless:— Pass. to be deprived of children, Anth.
G6590:
ἀτιμώρητος
unavenged, i. e.,
I. unpunished, ἀτ. γίγνεσθαι to escape punishment, Hdt., Thuc.:— adv. ‐τως, with impunity, Plat.
II. for which no revenge has been taken, ἀτιμώρητον ἐᾶν θάνατον Aeschin.
III. undefended, unprotected, Thuc.
G6591:
ἄτρακτος [Deriv. uncertain.]
I. a spindle, Hdt., Ar., etc.
II. an arrow, Soph.; cf. ἠλακάτη.
G6592:
ἀτραπός [τρέπω]
properly a path with no turnings, generally a path-way, road, Hom., Hdt., Thuc., etc.
G6595:
ἀττέλαβος [deriv. unkown]
a kind of locust without wings, Hdt.
G6596:
ἀτυχέω [ἀτυχής]
1. to be unlucky or unfortunate, fail, miscarry, Hdt., Thuc., etc.
2. c. gen., to fail of a thing, fail in getting or gaining it, τῆς ἀληθείας Xen.; so, c. part., Thuc.
3. ἀτ. πρός τινα to fail with another, i. e. to fail in one's request, Xen.:—Pass., τὰ ἀτυχηθέντα mischances, failures, Dem.
